excerpts.text: A bill of rights was overruled. -MORE- ADD ONE/BILL OF RIGHTS FAQS The Constitution was signed by 39 delegates on September 17, 1787, at the Pennsylvania State House, now known as Independence Hall, in Philadelphia.
After the Constitution was ratified in 1788, James Madison, who had already helped draft much of the original Constitution, took up the task of drafting a bill of rights.
Madison drafted 19 amendments, which he proposed to Congress on June 8, 1789.
These 12 were approved on September 25, 1789 and sent to the states for ratification.
The 10 amendments that are now known as the Bill of Rights were ratified on December 15, 1791, thus becoming a part of the Constitution.

The [drafting of the Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_drafting_and_ratification_of_the_United_States_Constitution "Timeline of drafting and ratification of the United States Constitution") by many of the nation's [Founding Fathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Founding_Fathers_of_the_United_States "Founding Fathers of the United States"), often referred to as its framing, was completed at the [Constitutional Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Convention_(United_States) "Constitutional Convention (United States)"), which assembled at [Independence Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_Hall "Independence Hall") in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") between May 25 and September 17, 1787.[[5]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMaier201027–28-8) Influenced by [English common law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_law "Common law") and the Enlightenment [liberalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberalism "Liberalism") of philosophers like [John Locke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Locke "John Locke") and [Montesquieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montesquieu "Montesquieu"), the Constitution's first three articles embody the doctrine of the [separation of powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Separation_of_powers "Separation of powers"), in which the federal government is divided into the [legislative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress"), [bicameral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicameralism "Bicameralism") Congress;[[d]](#cite_note-9) the [executive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States#Executive_branch "Federal government of the United States"), led by the [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States");[[e]](#cite_note-10) and the [judiciary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_judiciary_of_the_United_States "Federal judiciary of the United States"), within which the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States") has [apex jurisdiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_court "Supreme court").[[f]](#cite_note-11) Articles [IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_Four_of_the_United_States_Constitution "Article Four of the United States Constitution"), [V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_Five_of_the_United_States_Constitution "Article Five of the United States Constitution"), and [VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_Six_of_the_United_States_Constitution "Article Six of the United States Constitution") embody concepts of [federalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federalism "Federalism"), describing the rights and responsibilities of [state governments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_governments_of_the_United_States "State governments of the United States"), the [states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") in relationship to the [federal government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States "Federal government of the United States"), and the process of constitutional amendment. [Article VII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_Seven_of_the_United_States_Constitution "Article Seven of the United States Constitution") establishes the procedure used to [ratify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratify "Ratify") the constitution.

Since the Constitution became operational in 1789, it has been [amended](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_amendments_to_the_United_States_Constitution "List of amendments to the United States Constitution") 27 times.[[6]](#cite_note-12)[[7]](#cite_note-senategov-13) The first ten amendments, known collectively as the [Bill of Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Bill_of_Rights "United States Bill of Rights"), offer specific protections of individual liberty and justice and place restrictions on the powers of government within the U.S. states.[[8]](#cite_note-14)[[9]](#cite_note-15) Amendments 13–15 are known as the [Reconstruction Amendments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reconstruction_Amendments "Reconstruction Amendments").

On the appointed day, May 14, 1787, only the Virginia and Pennsylvania delegations were present, and the convention's opening meeting was postponed for lack of a quorum.[[29]](#cite_note-37) A quorum of seven states met on May 25, and deliberations began.

excerpts.text: | * [Drafting and ratification timeline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_drafting_and_ratification_of_the_United_States_Constitution "Timeline of drafting and ratification of the United States Constitution") * [Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_Convention_(United_States) "Constitutional Convention (United States)") * [Signing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signing_of_the_United_States_Constitution "Signing of the United States Constitution") * [Federalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federalism_in_the_United_States "Federalism in the United States") * [Republicanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republicanism_in_the_United_States "Republicanism in the United States") * [Bill of Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Bill_of_Rights) * [Reconstruction Amendments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reconstruction_Amendments "Reconstruction Amendments") |

The **United States Bill of Rights** comprises the first ten [amendments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_amendments_to_the_United_States_Constitution "List of amendments to the United States Constitution") to the [United States Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Constitution "United States Constitution"). It was proposed following the often bitter 1787–88 debate over the [ratification of the Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_drafting_and_ratification_of_the_United_States_Constitution "Timeline of drafting and ratification of the United States Constitution") and written to address the objections raised by [Anti-Federalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Federalism "Anti-Federalism"). The amendments of the Bill of Rights add to the Constitution specific guarantees of personal freedoms, such as [freedom of speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_speech_in_the_United_States "Freedom of speech in the United States"), the [right to publish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_the_press_in_the_United_States "Freedom of the press in the United States"), [practice religion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_religion_in_the_United_States "Freedom of religion in the United States"), [possess firearms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_to_keep_and_bear_arms_in_the_United_States "Right to keep and bear arms in the United States"), [to assemble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_to_assemble "Right to assemble"), and other [natural and legal rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_and_legal_rights "Natural and legal rights").

Largely because of the efforts of Representative [James Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Madison "James Madison"), who studied the deficiencies of the Constitution pointed out by Anti-Federalists and then crafted a series of corrective proposals, Congress approved twelve articles of amendment on September 25, 1789, and submitted them to the states for ratification. Contrary to Madison's proposal that the proposed amendments be incorporated into the main body of the Constitution (at the relevant articles and sections of the document), they were proposed as supplemental additions (codicils) to it.[[3]](#cite_note-3) Articles Three through Twelve were ratified as additions to the Constitution on December 15, 1791, and became Amendments One through Ten of the Constitution.

Madison drafted 19 amendments, which he proposed to Congress on June 8, 1789.
These 12 were approved on September 25, 1789, and sent to the states for ratification.
The 10 amendments that are now known as the Bill of Rights were ratified on December 15, 1791, and thus became part of the Constitution.

excerpts.text: On September 17, 1787, the Constitution was signed. As dictated by Article VII, the document would not become binding until it was ratified by nine of the 13 states. Beginning on December 7, five states—[Delaware](/topics/us-states/delaware), Pennsylvania, [New Jersey](/topics/us-states/new-jersey), [Georgia](/topics/us-states/georgia) and Connecticut—ratified it in quick succession.

On June 21, 1788, [New Hampshire](/topics/us-states/new-hampshire) became the ninth state to ratify the document, and it was subsequently agreed that government under the U.S. Constitution would begin on March 4, 1789.
